newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firmer on inflation, auction forecast.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firmer on inflation, auction forecast.

text.p: The Mexican peso opened firmer across the board on Tuesday in response to low inflation data released on Monday and forecast hikes in primary interest rates, dealers said.
"The market is looking at May inflation, which was in line with expectations," a trader said. "Most players want some pesos to play the debt market where rates are very attractive."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart opened 1.25 and 1.2 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9670/7.9700 and 7.9650/7.9680 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile begun the session 1.6 centavos firmer at 7.9560/7.9630 per dollar.

Banco de Mxico announced after the close of trade on Monday the consumer price index had risen by 0.91 percent in May, the first time it had done so by less than one percent in a month since the devaluation crisis of December 1994.
The central bank will hold its weekly auction of government securities on Tuesday evening. Money market dealers predicted gains on bellwether 28-day rates of more than 100 basis points.
"The market is somewhat long dollars and dealers want to shed some of them to reduce costs," another trader said.
Dealers said a stronger U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, up 5/32 in early trade to yield 6.81 percent, also bolstered the peso.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 7.9675/7.9775 per dollar for the 48-hour peso during the session.
